definitions.explanation: A book published as a single, independent volume rather than as part of a series, magazine, or periodical. In manga culture, refers to the collected volumes that compile chapters originally serialized in magazines.

examples.japanese: {単行本|たんこうぼん}が{出|で}た。
この{漫画|まんが}は{単行本|たんこうぼん}で{全|ぜん}20{巻|かん}ある。
examples.english: This manga has 20 collected volumes in total.

examples.japanese: {雑誌|ざっし}{連載|れんさい}を{読|よ}まずに{単行本|たんこうぼん}が{出|で}るまで{待|ま}つ{人|ひと}も{多|おお}い。
examples.english: Many people skip the magazine serialization and wait for the collected volume to come out.

notes:
COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {単行本|たんこうぼん}を{買|か}う (buy a collected volume)
- {単行本|たんこうぼん}が{出|で}る (a volume comes out)
- {単行本|たんこうぼん}{化|か} (being compiled into a volume)

USAGE:
In everyday conversation, {単行本|たんこうぼん} most often refers to manga volumes — the tankoubon format that collects several magazine chapters into one book. In publishing more broadly, it refers to any book published as a standalone volume, as opposed to a {文庫本|ぶんこぼん} (paperback) or {雑誌|ざっし} (magazine). Often abbreviated informally as タンコ.
